Hi Laura / Kim,

Thanks for taking the SIG/CAIQ follow-up call last week. As part of Brightline's SIG pack review we need a compact evidence portfolio showing your last authenticated vulnerability scan run, the remediation cadence you are committing to for critical/high CVEs, and a signed acceptance statement we can include in the auditor binder. Specifically, can you provide:

- The full authenticated scan report (Nessus/Qualys) for the most recent run (we have the July 8th export but the auditor asked for any scans since then).
- A short attestation (one page) that lists your SLA for Critical / High CVEs and who owns triage and verification.
- A link to the internal runbook describing patching/rollback steps and verification steps (or attach a sanitized excerpt).

Timing: the auditor would like these artifacts by end-of-week Jul 22 so they can complete the SIG evidence package. If a full report is sensitive, a redacted PDF plus MD5 hash of the original is fine — we just need provenance.

If you prefer, we can accept a signed PDF (DocuSign) of the attestation and a Drive link for the scan PDF.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — let me know if any of the asks are a problem.

Thanks,
Anita Rao

Anita — thanks for the clear checklist. See items below and attached files. I kept the packet concise to avoid exposing internal hostnames; happy to provide the full scan under an NDA if needed.

Summary of deliverables (attached):
- redwood-vm-scan-20280715.pdf — redacted authenticated scan export (vulnerability IDs, severity, remediation status).
- cve-acceptance-letter-Redwood-20280721.pdf — signed attestation from our security ops lead describing SLA commitments.
- runbook-patch-process-20280718.md — sanitized excerpt of the patch/rollback verification runbook.

Key commitments (short):
- Critical CVEs: mitigation/patch plan created within 24 hours of detection; code/infra patching completed within 14 calendar days (exceptions routed to exec review).
- High CVEs: mitigation plan within 72 hours; remediation within 30 calendar days.
- Verification: triage owner validates fix in staging and signs off before production promotion. Verification is tracked in JIRA (project VM-OPS).

Provenance and integrity: the attached PDF has an MD5 footer with the original export id (scan-export-20280715-4492). Full unredacted findings are available via secure transfer if the auditor requires hashes or a notarized copy.

Links / references: Drive folder (view-only) — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwood-VM-Evidence. HubSpot evidence record HS-00098765 is also updated with the packet.

If that looks good, please confirm and we will produce a DocuSign copy of the attestation for your binder.

Anita / Laura — quick clarification on SLAs and exceptions so it's explicit for the auditor: 

- SLA windows are measured in calendar days from the time a vulnerability is confirmed and assigned to an owner.
- For third-party library CVEs that require coordinated upstream fixes, our mitigation window follows the same owner-assigned dates, but remediation timelines may be committed as a staged rollout (e.g., hotfix + follow-up patch) — we document those in the remediation ticket.
- Emergency exceptions (where patching would materially break production) are escalated to the CTO/Head of Ops and recorded in our incident ledger; we include compensating controls (network ACLs, WAF rules) until the patch lands.

I'll add a one-line clarification to the attestation PDF and re-upload a DocuSign-enabled copy if you want it signed by both Security Ops and Engineering.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
